book_title: Chapter 9: Bull vs. Bear, Likely Outcomes & Our Action Plan
question: Weighing both the AI silicon bull case and the dilution/Stage 4 bear case, what is our independent verdict, holding action, and 100% capital redeployment plan?

epigraph.quote: The stock market is a no-called-strike game. You don't have to swing at everything—you can wait for your pitch.
epigraph.author: Warren Buffett

web_blocks.title: 9.1 Steelmanning Both Sides of the Aisle

web_blocks.html: The Honest Bull Case: AMD is executing a historic semiconductor turnaround. Under Lisa Su, EPYC server CPUs reached 46.2% revenue share against Intel. Q3 2026 Data Center sales surged +97% YoY to $8.55 billion at a 33.7% operating margin [2][3]. Q4 2026 guidance sits near $17.0 billion (+66% YoY) [3]. Six-gigawatt MI450 deals with OpenAI and Meta, plus ZT Systems, World Labs, and Taalas, build a full-stack rival to NVIDIA [2][15][24]. Clean execution could lift FY2027 revenue past $95B and push shares toward $540.

The Honest Bear Case: Strong engineering does not protect buyers from bad entry points or heavy dilution. First, Pass 1 grades AMD CYCLICAL_CONDITIONAL. GAAP EBIT fell 89% in FY2023, GAAP ROIC sits near 5.6% to 9.9%, and China accounts for 22.4% of revenue [1][2][27]. Acquisition goodwill and intangibles exceed $40.6B and will climb past $50B after World Labs and Taalas [2]. Second, AMD took on $81.8 billion in off-balance-sheet obligations alongside $11.46 billion in inventory (an EY Critical Audit Matter) [1][2]. On November 23, Form S-3ASR registered 336.93 million resale shares (~20.5% dilution) [26]. Third, NVIDIA trades at 8.66x Forward P/E with 74.9% gross margins and 74.2% ROIC, while AMD trades at 21.51x Forward P/E in Stage 4 [27][28][33].

Weighing both sides against the primary SEC record and November 24 market structure yields a negative expected return at $387.65. Our probability-weighted 12-month expected value is $349.50 (-9.8% vs. CMP), with Base fair value ($375.00) sitting below current market price. Even if AMD falls to our $335.00–$355.00 watch shelf (with a $295.00 structural invalidation floor), upside to $375.00 Base offers just 0.33:1 reward-to-risk—failing our 1.50:1 hurdle and mandating a clean REJECTED verdict rather than a timid hedge.

web_blocks.html: Three-Horizon Independent Verdict: Over the Short Term (1–3 months), our verdict is Stay Away / REJECTED. Stage 4 momentum, a $46.51 ATR, and 2.1% sector breadth leave zero long edge. Over the Medium Term (6–18 months), we stay REJECTED on the Sidelines. AMD must prove that its $81.8B commitment stack and 336.9M-share resale shelf translate into clean cash flow rather than write-downs. Over the Long Term (3–5 years), AMD is a Conditional Compounder to revisit only after a Stage 1 base, a Stage 2 breakout, and >=1.50:1 diluted asymmetry.

book_paragraphs: We have reached the moment of truth. After ten years of financial forensics, a deep dive into every silicon segment, a hard look at November's 336.9-million-share S-3ASR filing, and a cold read of the Stage 4 chart, you and I have to make an unambiguous call.

I respect what Lisa Su and her engineers have built. Taking EPYC to 46% server CPU revenue share and guiding Q4 2026 revenue to $17 billion is an extraordinary operational feat. If you only read the headline press releases, you would want to back up the truck on a 41% pullback.

But institutional investing is not about applauding great engineering—it is about protecting your capital against asymmetric downside. Right now, AMD asks you to accept three simultaneous hazards: a cyclical business that just took on $81.8 billion in off-balance-sheet commitments, a 20.5% potential dilution wave registered for resale on November 23, and a violent Stage 4 breakdown where 98% of semiconductor stocks are underwater. Meanwhile, NVIDIA and Broadcom offer vastly superior margins and ROIC at half the forward multiple.

Our independent verdict is REJECTED on Valuation and Trend. Since you hold zero shares of AMD across Schwab and Robinhood, your holding action is NOT_HELD, and your best move with marginal cash is keeping 100% in USD reserves while the S&P 500 works through its ten-distribution-day Downtrend. We will park AMD on our monitored discard radar with four clear re-entry gates. Remember Buffett's rule: there are no called strikes in investing. Let this pitch go by, keep your powder dry, and wait for a Stage 2 setup where the math and the tape are both on your side.

Before we lock our final decision, let us sit on both sides of the investment committee table and give each side its strongest, fairest voice. If you are arguing the Bull Case today, you have real ammunition. AMD is no longer a scrappy PC chipmaker hoping Intel stumbles. EPYC has conquered nearly half of x86 server CPU revenue. Q3 2026 Data Center revenue surged 97% year over year to $8.55 billion with 33.7% operating margins, and Q4 guidance of $17.0 billion signals accelerating hyperscaler pull-through. With ZT Systems rack engineering, OpenAI and Meta 6-gigawatt commitments, World Labs spatial AI, and Taalas single-model inference chips, AMD is building a full-stack alternative to NVIDIA. If those racks ship smoothly in 2027 and 2028, AMD could clear $95 billion in revenue and earn $18 per diluted share, justifying our $540 Bull Case target.

Now slide across the table and steelman the Bear Case with equal rigor. Why did our price-blind Pass 1 audit grade AMD CYCLICAL_CONDITIONAL instead of COMPOUNDER_PASS? Because semiconductor history is littered with companies that looked invincible at peak backlog right before working capital and dilution bit back. In FY2023, AMD's GAAP operating income collapsed 89% from its FY2021 peak. Today, GAAP ROIC still hovers in the mid-to-high single digits under $40.6 billion of acquisition goodwill and intangibles—soon climbing past $50 billion after World Labs and Taalas. To win hyperscaler GPU share, AMD committed to $81.8 billion in off-balance-sheet supplier orders, data center leases, credit guarantees, and cloud backstops, while carrying $11.46 billion in inventory flagged by Ernst & Young as a Critical Audit Matter. And on November 23, AMD registered 336.93 million resale and warrant shares—a 20.5% potential dilution wave—right as the stock broke into Stage 4.

When we weight those three outcomes honestly—30% Bear ($180), 50% Base ($375), and 20% Bull ($540)—the probability-weighted expected value is $349.50, or -9.8% below today's $387.65 close. That settles our anti-hedging test cleanly. We do not hide behind a vague 'Hold' or a timid 'Wait for Support' when even the $335–$355 watch shelf offers just 0.33-to-1 reward-to-risk against our $375 Base value and $295 structural stop. The honest, evidence-derived verdict for new capital is REJECTED (TIER_0) on VALUATION and TREND.

Now let us translate that verdict directly into your portfolio and your shortlist request. First, checking the verified November 24 positions ledger confirms you hold zero shares of AMD across both Charles Schwab and Robinhood, so your current holding action is NOT_HELD with zero shares to sell. Second, you asked to add AMD to your shortlist. Under our deterministic pipeline rules, a REJECTED / TIER_0 underwriting routes to the monitored discard ledger rather than the active shortlist, keeping your active buy queue strictly reserved for Stage 2 setups with genuine asymmetry. AMD stays on permanent radar with four concrete re-evaluation gates: an S&P 500 Downtrend exit plus a multi-week Stage 1 base and future flattening 30-week SMA reclaim on volume, inventory growth slowing below revenue growth, clean absorption of the S-3ASR supply overhang, and at least 1.50-to-1 diluted reward-to-risk.

Finally, where should your next marginal dollar go instead? Your consolidated US portfolio sits at $83,506.98—$61,337.64 in equities, $14,878.43 in options, and $7,290.91 in cash (8.73% of net worth). Because the S&P 500 is in a ten-distribution-day Downtrend with just 27.8% of stocks above their 50-day average and the 10-Year Treasury at 4.92%, our Downtrend target cash floor is 22%. That means 100.0% of marginal USD capital belongs in cash reserves today. We benchmarked your best Stage 2 shortlist candidate—PepsiCo (PEP, $144.98 TV / $142.68 daily ledger, 1.92:1 support R:R, currently RESEARCH_REQUIRED)—and a clean Stage 2 outside software leader—Automatic Data Processing (ADP, $317.78, 26.6% operating margin, but $308.40 consensus target below CMP)—and kept both at 0.0% until breadth heals and liquidity rebuilds. Protecting cash in a Stage 4 washout is how you stay ready to buy the real leaders when Stage 2 returns.

book_callouts.title: NARRATOR'S REFLECTION: Discipline Beats Heroism
book_callouts.text: Passing on a famous AI name after a 41% drop feels uncomfortable—that is exactly why discipline pays. Great businesses bought during Stage 4 breakdowns with $81.8B in off-balance-sheet risk and 336.9M overhang shares can easily fall another 35% before they base.
